reason: Premise holds and no better shape survived, so keep this PR and fix it before merge: on 1.4.3-canary.1+367d939d9 and on the base build I reproduced both failures (delete an `npm:` override with bun.lock kept and the fork stays installed and pinned, exit 0, "no changes"; a bun.lock rejected after its overrides installs the alias target under the plain name, or exits 1 with `GET <registry>/ - 404`), the PR build installs the registry package in each, and across seven install test files the two builds differ only in the PR's 17 new tests (6/17 on base, 17/17 on the PR build; one 5 s timeout under a load average near 650 passed on every re-run). No user reported it (reach, tracker-history, existence), but the no-demand rule does not send it to close or supersede: the result is a silently wrong package on a shipped build, the source change is +107/-67 in 12 files, draft #36476 has been idle since 2026-08-04, and #43375 and #43515 are open without review. Required first, from the four should-fix premise concerns: (bigger-shape) make the migrations enforce the rule instead of a hand-written `None`, by narrowing `Migrator.manager` and `migrate_packages` at /workspace/bun/src/install/migration/npm_lock.rs:103 and :122 to `&PackageManager` (the uses at :136, :360 and :556 only read; I did not compile this), adding to /workspace/bun/test/cli/install/migration/migrate.test.ts a yarn.lock that bun reads and does not use (`bun add` with no root dependencies gives exit 1 with "Registry URL must be http:// or https://" on base and exit 0 on the PR build, and no test covers it), and guarding the row sites of /workspace/bun/src/install/yarn.rs with a source lint or test; (bigger-shape) close or state the `$name` override path through `OverrideMap::parse_append` at npm_lock.rs:1028 and yarn.rs:1989, and retitle to "lockfile loaders do not register npm: aliases" with the remaining writers listed; (existence) drop the claim that npm takes overrides from the manifest (npm 11.16.0 prints "up to date" and keeps a locked fork), list the deleted-override flip as a behaviour change and pin it with a test of that exact flow in /workspace/bun/test/cli/install/bun-lock.test.ts. In the body also say that no user reported it and that it does not fix #23264, name #43375 (it has its own `known_npm_aliases.clear()` and rebuild) with one membership rule and the merge order, ask for #43515 first, and add the `resolutions` and `pnpm.overrides` reader-gap scenarios with links to #38811 and #38754 (already-planned, tracker-history, bigger-shape); whether a kept bun.lockb keeps registering its dependency rows is the install maintainer's call and not a blocker (existence); not verified by me: the full suite, rust:check-all, a debug or ASAN build, and the `$name` case (probes are in /tmp/disposition-probe/).
